extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for requesting or imposing suspension or deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103 (applicant-requested suspension, CPA/RCE suspensions, deferral under 1.103(d), and Office-initiated suspensions). Includes required forms, fees, limits, and effects on prosecution and patent term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action — applicability and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will suspend action in an application if it has accepted a request to publish a statutory invention registration in the application; suspension applies to an impending Office action by the examiner and not to applicant replies. Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in patent term adjustment accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703 equal to the number of days beginning on the date the request was filed and ending on the date of termination (see 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse suspension of action (Office delaying examiner action) with extension of time for reply (37 CFR 1.136). Action cannot be suspended in an application which contains an outstanding Office action or requirement awaiting reply by the applicant. Where a suspension is granted, the applicant is required to notify the examiner and request continuance of prosecution or a further suspension at the end of the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.103(a) — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must: (A) be presented as a separate paper; (B) be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g); (C) request a specific and reasonable period of suspension not greater than 6 months; and (D) present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requirements of 37 CFR 1.103(a) are not met, the application will be taken up for action. A petition to suspend to allow time to submit an information disclosure statement will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons (37 CFR 1.97 provides adequate recourse). In new applications, merely including a request on a transmittal form letter is insufficient; consider filing a deferral under 1.103(d) if appropriate. Use form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.54) to notify grant or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request under 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) — CPA/RCE suspension requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(b) or (c) for a period not exceeding three months in a continued prosecution application (CPA) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design applications) or in a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114; the request must be filed at the time of filing the CPA or RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not grant the requested suspension unless: (A) the request is filed with the filing of a design CPA or an RCE (use the check box on PTO/SB/29 or PTO/SB/30 or submit separately); (1) if filed with an RCE, the RCE must comply with 37 CFR 1.114 (submission and fee under 1.17(e)); (2) if filed with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA; (B) the request specifies the period in whole months (maximum 3 months). If no period is specified or it exceeds 3 months, the Office will assume 3 months; and (C) the request includes the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i). If the CPA/RCE is improper (no filing date, missing submission/fee), the request will not be recognized and action will not be suspended. If the request is improper (untimely, missing fee), the Office will deny suspension and process the CPA/RCE (see form ¶ 7.56.01). A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within the suspension period (see MPEP § 714.03(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for deferral under 37 CFR 1.103(d) — requirements and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In new applications, applicants may request a deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119/120/121/365. The request must be filed before the Office issues an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance, and the suspension starts when the Office grants the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/37 may be used. A request for deferral must include: (A) a period of suspension in whole months not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date (Office will assume maximum if omitted or excessive); (B) the publication fee under 37 CFR 1.18(d); and (C) the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). The Office will not grant deferral unless: (A) the application is an original utility or plant application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or a national stage after compliance with 1.495 (not a design, reissue, or CPA); (B) the application was filed on or after Nov. 29, 2000; (C) no nonpublication request under 1.213(a) is on file (or applicant rescinds it under 1.213(b)); (D) the application is in condition for publication per 1.211(c); and (E) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151. Supervisory patent examiner approval is required for grant. Use form paragraphs (¶ 7.54.01/¶ 7.54.02) to notify applicant of grant/denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request termination of a suspension of action prior to the end of the suspension period; the request is effective when an appropriate Office official acts on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the termination request properly identifies the application and the suspension period has not expired when the Office acts, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner’s docket. An acknowledgment should be sent to applicant using form paragraph ¶ 7.54.02. Insert the filing date of the termination request and the number of months for the deferral/grant where indicated in the form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension — limits, approvals, and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action on its own initiative (37 CFR 1.103(e)), but such suspensions should be avoided if possible. Every Office-initiated suspension will be limited to a maximum period of 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may grant an initial suspension on his/her own initiative for a maximum of 6 months. Upon expiration the examiner should take up action or evaluate possibilities for giving an action on the merits (e.g., find alternative references). If a second or subsequent suspension is necessary, the Technology Center (TC) Director’s approval is required and the TC Director’s signature must appear on the suspension notification (see MPEP § 1003). Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(f) is decided by the TC Director of work group 3640. Use form paragraphs such as ¶ 7.52 (Awaiting New Reference) and ¶ 7.53 (Possible Interference) for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply will be entered if it is filed within the period during which action is suspended by the Office under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or 1.103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03(a) regarding the treatment of supplemental replies during suspension. A supplemental reply filed during an Office suspension may be entered and considered as appropriate (procedural rules for entry apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA/RCE or improper suspension request — consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or RCE is improper (no filing date or RCE filed without a submission or fee), or the request for suspension is improper (untimely or without the processing fee under 1.17(i)), the Office will not recognize the request for suspension and action will not be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of improper CPA or RCE will be sent as appropriate. The time period set in the previous Office communication (e.g., a final Office action or a notice of allowance) continues to run from the mailing date of that communication. If the applicant later files a proper RCE or CPA, the request for suspension should be resubmitted to ensure processing. If a suspension request is improper, the Office will process the CPA/RCE and place the application on the examiner’s docket and notify applicant of the denial using form paragraph ¶ 7.56.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum suspension durations and patent-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum periods: petition under 1.103(a) — up to 6 months; requests tied to CPA or RCE under 1.103(b)/(c) — up to 3 months; deferral under 1.103(d) — up to 3 years from earliest effective filing date. Office-initiated suspensions are limited to a maximum of 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in any patent term adjustment accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703 equal to the number of days the suspension is in effect (see 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1)). Applicants should be aware that suspension increases pendency and may shorten effective patent term; weigh the consequences before requesting deferral or suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension not allowed while applicant reply is outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Action cannot be suspended in an application which contains an outstanding Office action or requirement awaiting reply by the applicant; only action by the examiner can be suspended under 37 CFR 1.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an outstanding Office action or requirement is awaiting applicant reply, a request for suspension under 1.103(a) will be denied as improper (see form ¶ 7.56). Examiners should be aware that suspension affects the examiner’s docketing, not applicant’s time for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing form, fee, and signature requirements for deferral requests (PTO/SB/37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/37 (Request for Deferral of Examination 37 CFR 1.103(d)) may be used to request deferral; the request must indicate months (maximum 3 years), include processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) and publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)), and must include signatures of all inventors or assignees of record (or their representatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form warns that information may become public and that credit card information should not be included on the form. The form includes instructions about payment (deposit account, check, PTO-2038). The Office will assume the maximum period requested if none or an excessive period is specified. Note privacy and PRA statements and where to send comments on paperwork burden. Failure to include required fees will render the request improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern — requests to suspend solely to allow IDS submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action to allow applicant time to submit an information disclosure statement will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.97 provides adequate recourse for timely submission of prior art for consideration by the examiner; do not use suspension petitions as a substitute for IDS procedures.
